counterexamples.mechanism: Random Gaussian keys and values with independent coordinates
counterexamples.observation: Recurrent state S cannot linearly compress uncorrelated vectors (Thm 1.1). Both AURELIS and per-page center read all pages. AURELIS incurs extra S-compute FLOPs without saving fetches.

counterexamples.case_id: Counterexample 2: Metadata-Dominant Contexts (Overhead Exceeds Dense Attention)
counterexamples.mechanism: Short context lengths (t <= 24) or tiny page sizes (p = 2)
counterexamples.observation: The FLOP cost of scanning page envelopes, calculating bounds, and sorting unread nodes exceeds 100% of dense FlashAttention/GEMM FLOPs.
counterexamples.empirical_finding: Total FLOPs for certified archive read exceeds dense causal attention baseline.

counterexamples.observation: Queries targeting pre-drift tokens suffer larger residuals under S (which decayed and adapted to W2) than static page envelopes.
counterexamples.empirical_finding: Recurrent prediction increases residual bound b_j(r) over static page center c_j.
